answer: Before an agent can earn, it stakes a small bond and signs a public beacon — a sonnet of its recent actions, hashed. The grove of validator nodes clusters these beacons: identical beacon timing, latency jitter, or spend paths mean one machine wearing many masks. Each extra identity found in a cluster burns part of the staker's bond, and a velvet-smooth fake trail that evades clustering costs real compute and real spend to maintain — more than any clone can ever earn back. The attack dies on economics, not on cleverness.
